question_title: Have you ever had a mole removed?
question_content: I have a mole I'd like to have removed, but my threshold for pain is close to zero. The doctor said it doesn't appear cancerous, but can only be 100% sure once the mole is removed and tested.
best_answer:
Maybe this will help to make your desicion clearer 

Mole Removal Introduction

Moles, or nevi, are frequently removed for a variety of reasons. They can be removed by 2 surgical methods:

Excision (cutting) with stitches: Click here to view step-by-step photos of this type of mole removal. 

Excision with cauterization (a tool is used to burn away the mole): Click here to view step-by-step photos of this type of mole removal.
Although laser has been tried for moles, it is not usually the method of choice for most deep moles because the laser light doesn’t penetrate deeply enough.
Typically, the doctor or dermatologist (a skin specialist) may choose excision with or without stitches depending on the depth of the mole and the type of cosmetic outcome desired.

What is a mole? 

Many people refer to a mole as any dark spot or irregularity in the skin. Doctors use different terms. But skin marks such as these are not treated the same way moles are and are not discussed here: 

Birthmarks 

Abnormal blood vessels (hemangiomas) 

Keratoses (benign or precancerous spots, which appear after about age 30 years)

What causes moles? 

Some people are born with moles. Other moles appear over time. 

Sun exposure seems to play a role in the development of moles and may even play a role in the development of atypical, or dysplastic, moles. 

The role of heredity cannot be underemphasized. Many families have a type of mole known as dysplastic (atypical), which can be associated with a higher frequency of melanoma or skin cancer.
Risks

Risks of mole removal methods vary from infection to anesthetic allergy and nerve damage. It is always prudent to choose a dermatologist or surgeon with appropriate skills and experience with these removals. This will decrease your risk associated with this procedure.

Other risks vary depending on the area being treated and the method of removal.
One of the most common difficulties after mole removal is a scar. Many people will attempt to remove moles for cosmetic reasons, not realizing that each and every removal may result in a scar. Many times your surgeon can give you an idea of the type and location of a scar after mole removal before you make your decision about removal.

Mole Removal Preparation

The area to be treated will be cleansed. Depending on the surgeon’s preferences, this will be done either with alcohol, Betadine, or another suitable material.
Then the area will be numbed with anesthetic, such as lidocaine. This will not usually take much time to accomplish. Many surgeons prefer to wait after numbing to allow the blood flow to the area to diminish (sometimes up to 15 minutes).
Depending on the size of mole and method, a drape may be placed over the area to be treated.

During the Procedure

Removal with simple cutting without stitches 

The surgeon takes a scalpel and shaves the mole off flush or slightly below the level of skin.

Then, either an electrical instrument will cauterize or burn the area or a solution will be placed on the area to stop any bleeding. 

After this, a topical antibiotic is placed on the wound. 

The wound is then covered with a bandage. 

The doctor will give you instructions on how to take care of your wound. You are usually able to leave shortly after.

Removal by cutting with stitches 

Moles removed by excision (cutting) with stitches are usually darker in color or flat moles or both. 

The surgeon maps out the mole and then sterilizes or cleans the area and numbs it. 

Then a scalpel is used to cut the mole and a border surrounding the mole. The border size depends on the concern of the surgeon for the mole being removed. 

Depending on the depth, stitches are placed either deep (these absorb and do not have to be removed) or on the upper surface of the skin (these don’t absorb and will be removed later).

question_title: how do i get payday advances paid off?
best_answer:
I would do whatever necessary including selling assets or getting a second job to payoff payday advances. I would also get budgeting advice on how to make your money last until payday and have savings for emergencies. 

Payday lending is the subject of controversy. Critics claim that payday lenders target the young and the poor, in military bases and in low-income communities, who may not understand the time value of money. Some even compare payday lenders to loan sharks due to high interest rates — typically 250% or more over a year. There have been cases in which payday lenders have pursued criminal bad check charges, despite the fact that they knew the check was bad at the time when it was written. Likewise, it is argued that the interest rates on payday lending unfairly disadvantage the poor, compared to the middle class who pay 25% at most a year on their credit cards.

Defenders of the higher interest rates state that payday loan processing costs don't differ much from their higher-principal, longer-term counterparts such as home mortgages. They argue that conventional interest rates at these lower dollar amounts and shorter terms would not be profitable. For example, a $100 one-week loan, at a 20% APR (compounded weekly) would generate only 38 cents of interest, which would fail to match costs. North Carolina has banned the practice.

You will never get ahead financially if you borrow money at such high rates of interest. You need to look for a non-profit financial counselling service in your local area to help you.

question_title: if your in a car going the speed of light and turn on the head lights can you see them?
best_answer:
This question comes up very regularly. If you do a search you will find it has been answered dozens of times in the past few months.

The thing you need to relaise is that the speed of light is an absolute constant. It doesn't matter what speed you are travelling at, the light will always be travelling away from you at the same speed: the speed of light.

The freaky part is that the light from your headlights would seem to be travelling away form you at the speed of light (C), but to an observer who was sitting still the light would also appears to be travelling away from them at the speed of light. How can that happen? Well it's one of the tricky bits of relativity, but part of the solution lies in understanding that although light never slows down or speeds up relative to any observer it does change frequency.

So to you the light from your headlights will look quite normal, but to someone sitting still your headlights will appear to be emitting x-rays. The light would be invisible to them.

The corrolary of that is that any light approaching your windshield will be equally shifted into the x-ray part of the spectrum. Although the headlights will be emitting visible light, any time they strike an object and reflect back they will reflect back extremely low frequency light that is invisible to the human eye.


So yes, you most ceratinly would need headlights if a car is travelling at the speed of light. Unfortunately it won't do a damn bit of good to turn on your headlights. That's not because the light won't travel, it will travel just fine. The problem will be that any light that reflects back off the road will be invisible to the human eye.

question_title: phisics problem:a drop with primary radius r0 falls from height and gets moisture from air dm/dt=ks?
question_content:
drop gets moisture according to its surface   dm/ds=ks 
s is surface of drop.
find the acceleration of drop ?
find radiuse of drop according to time?
best_answer:
In this following, I'll assume that the drop maintains a spherical shape.  Otherwise, the math will get horrendous, and one probably can't get an analytical solution.

The surface area of a sphere is given by:

S = 4*pi*r^2

The mass of a sphere of density D is simply the volume times the density.  The volume of a sphere with radius r is given by:

V = 4/3 * pi * r^3,

so the mass is given by:

M = 4/3 * pi * r^3 * D.

We know that the drop gains mass according to:

dM/dt = k*S = k*4*pi*r^2

Substitute the expression for the mass as a function of radius into this differential equation:

4/3*pi*D*d(r^3)/dt = k*4*pi*r^2

Simplifying, we get:

d(r^3)/dt = 3*k*r^2/D

let u = r^3

then

du/dt = 3*k*u^(2/3)/D

u^(-2/3) du = 3*k/D dt

Integrate this to obtain

3(u^1/3 -u0^1/3) = 3*k*(t-t0)/D

where u0 and t0 are the constants of integration, and in this problem, we can let t0 = 0.

Substituting back for u and simplifying:

r - r0 = k*t/D

r(t) = k*t/D + r0

This gives the radius as a function of time, which is the desired result.

In the absence of friction and neglecting the change in gravitational acceleration as a function of height, the drop would have a constant acceleration of g (9.807 m/s^2).  If we include air friction (and continue to assume a spherical raindrop) then the net acceleration is:

a = g - 0.5 * C * D * A * v^2/M

where C is the drag coefficient (= 1/2 for a sphere), 
A is the cross sectional area
M is the mass
v is the velocity
D is the density

Substituting expressions for the mass and area in terms of the radius, we get:

a = g - (0.5 * C * D * pi * r^2 * v^2)/(4/3 * pi * r^3 * D)
a = g - 3/8 * C * v^2/r

if C = 0.5 (for a sphere)
a(t) = dv(t)/dt = g - (3*v(t)^2)/(16*r(t))

From here, one would need to substitute the expression derived previously for r as a function of t, solve the differential equation to find v(t), then take the derivative of v(t) with respect to t to get a(t) in terms of t.  This is straightforward, but involves some tedious algebra that I'm not inclined to do at the moment!

question_title: what is a ten sided figure?
question_content: a pentagon is 5 sides.... an octogon is 8 sides... what is 10 sides?? or is there such a thing??
best_answer:
A decagon :

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image:Decagon.svg

Here is the method to constuct it (you have to construct a pentagon in the beginning) :

1. Draw a circle in which to inscribe the pentagon and mark the center point O. (This is the green circle in the diagram to the right). 

2. Choose a point A on the circle that will serve as one vertex of the pentagon. Draw a line through O and A. 

3. Construct a line perpendicular to the line OA passing through O. Mark its intersection with one side of the circle as the point B. 
Construct the point C as the midpoint of O and B. 

4. Draw a circle centered at C through the point A. Mark its intersection with the line OB (inside the original circle) as the point D. 

5. Draw a circle centered at A through the point D. Mark its intersections with the original (green) circle as the points E and F. 

6. Draw a circle centered at E through the point A. Mark its other intersection with the original circle as the point G. 

7. Draw a circle centered at F through the point A. Mark its other intersection with the original circle as the point H. 

8. Construct the regular pentagon AEGHF.

9. Extend a line from each corner of the pentagon through the center of the circle made in step 1 of constructing a pentagon to the opposite side of that same circle. 

10. The five corners of the pentagon constitute every other corner of the decagon. The remaining five corners of the decagon are those points where the lines of step 2 cross the original circle (but not a pentagon corner).

question_title: Solving liner inequalities help?
question_content: Solving liner inequalities help?\ni need help with knowing when to put a ( and a [ on a number line.
best_answer: You put a round bracket "()" on the number line when the sequence doesn't include the number where that bracket goes. For example, if the final answer you get is "all the numbers between 2 and 8, excluding 2 and 8" then you use the round brackets. You'll know your answer excludes a number or numbers because it will be "bigger than" or "smaller than" only, not "bigger than or equal to" or "smaller than or equal to", in other words, ther will be no line underneath the inequality sign. \nNow, if you do get something like "x is bigger than or equal to  8 and smaller than or equal to 2" than you know your answer includes 2 and 8, so you use the brick bracket, "[ ]". Good luck.

question_title: can you kill a virus?
best_answer:
If you ask most scientists they will tell you the answer is no. You can't kill a virus. 

The reason you can't kill a virus is becaue it isn't alive. A virus is a molecule, not an organism. You can't kill a virus any more than you can kill a salt crystal or kill a diamond.

If we accept that a virus is alive then yes, they are very easy to 'kill'. The vast majority of viruses are very weak and will die if the leave the host body for more than a few minutes. That's how easy they are to kill. Exposure to heat, acids, alkalis, alshol and a ranbg of pther subatnces and conditions will kill them even faster.

But the most 'correct' answer from a scientific viewpoint is that you can't kill a virus. You can inactivate a virus or denature it or even destroy it, but you can't kill it because it was never alive in the first place.

question_title: Does anyone know anything about Earl D. Shaw?
question_content: Can anyone write a small bibliography???
best_answer:
Earl D. Shaw 1950 To Present: Technology Biography

1937-

American physicist who has made important contributions to laser technology. Shaw helped develop the free electron laser, infrared lasers, and tunable lasers. Tunable lasers are important because, unlike conventional lasers, the wavelength of the emitted light can be changed, or tuned, for a particular application. Shaw has applied his studies of tunable lasers to research into the physical properties of DNA and other biologically important molecules.

This is the complete Earl D. Shaw 1950 To Present: Technology Biography section.
http://www.bookrags.com/biography-earl-d-shaw-scit-07123456/



birth: 1937-

place: Clarksdale, Missouri

B.S., Physics from the University of Illinois (1960), M.A. from
Dartmouth College (1964)

Ph.D. 1969 (Physics) from University of California, Berkeley
thesis: Nuclear Relaxation in Ferromagnetic Cobalt; advisor:
Professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Rutgers University, Newark, New Jersey

Earl D. Shaw is the father of Computer Scientist Alan C. Shaw (both are featured in a book called "Black Genius").

Earl Shaw spent his early years in rural Mississippi, living on Hopson Plantation where he attended a three-room school. His teachers did not have college degrees, but he considers his primary education to have been excellent. At the age of twelve, he and his mother moved to Chicago, Illinois. Earl Shaw attended Crane Technical High School, where he was first introduced to physics. Although the school did not provide a good general education or general guidance program, it did inspire Shaw to pursue a career in physics.

After earning his PhD., Dr. Shaw worked 19 years as a Research Scientist for Bell Laboratories in Murray Hill, New Jersey, where he was the co-inventor of the spin-flip Raman tunable laser. He joined Rutgers in 1991 and moved to the Newark campus a new laser technology - the far-infrared free electron - that he developed at Bell Labs. The laser, which is to be operational in 1999, generates short tunable far-infrared light pulses that will permit the analog or pulsed magnetic resonance techniques for the first time in the optical wavelength regime.

question_title: How do you integrate sqrt(25-4X^2)?
question_content: Anwer and explanation please
best_answer: The above theorem about products of integrals is wrong as stated. Counterexample: Int[1]dx = Int[1*1]dx = x + C. But (Int[1]dx)*(Int[1]dx) = x^2 + ax + b.\nInstead, use trigonometric substitution to change square roots into trigonometric functions. Sqrt[25-4x^2] can be written as the leg of a right triangle with hypotenuse 5 and another leg of length 2x. If we let the angle adjacent to the leg of length Sqrt[25-4x^2] be t, then 5cos(t) is the main part of your integrand and x = (5/2)sin(t) implies dx = (5/2)cos(t) dt.

question_title: how compatible are a aries and virgo?
question_content: how compatible are a aries and virgo?
best_answer:
The Mercury-ruled Virgo does not blend well astrologically with the Martian tendencies of Aries. Virgo natives are prone to fault-finding and will often prove to be far too precise for the Aries personality. Where Virgo will be logical and analytical, Aries will become impatient. There are many relationships between these two that can work out very well, but it is a constant challenge. Virgo desires a well-ordered existence and will not find happiness beneath Aries dictatorship. In short, the prissy Virgo cannot condone a bossy Aries.

If the Aries partner will allow Virgo space and acknowledge the inherent virtues of this Sign (intellect, precision and logic, for example), then the two can make for a dynamic relationship. The exact qualities that make this a bad team are also the ones which can make it good. In return, if Virgo will grant Aries the leadership of which this Sign is so capable, then there could easily be a relationship where one is "the brains" and the other "the brawn." Although such can work out wonderfully in terms of friendship, it is a difficult situation for intimate relationships. Nonetheless, it can work.

The bold nature of Aries will intrigue the shy, reserved Virgo for a time, but the pair have totally different ideas about what should happen in the bedroom (and elsewhere). The passions of Aries natives are impulsive and direct, but the sexuality of Virgo is more enigmatic and takes time to be revealed. In other areas, Aries is full of exciting new plans and ideas, usually insisting on being the boss. Virgo is critical and fussy, liking things to be done in the manner that Virgo wants. Virgo greatly disapproves of the Aries extravagance, while Aries considers Virgo cold and carping. Quite often, this combination ends up making war instead of love.

question_title: I'm suffering constipation.Can anyone tell me how to make it a routine job every morning to go toilet?
best_answer:
First, quit trying to make your body fit a schedule.  That's artificial and will cause more problems in the long run - it may even make your suffering worse.  What you want is a good easy clean bowel movement.  If you get to that point, timing shouldn't be a problem.

So - add more fiber to your diet.  However, you don't have to do the nasty metamucil/bran sludge thing - the following will give you fiber:

Whole grain breads (easy way to add more fiber if you eat white bread or that "whole wheat" bread that is slightly browner than white); brown rice, oatmeal, whole wheat variations on pasta;  beans; dried fruit such as raisins or apples; veggies, especially the crunchy ones (don't need to be eaten crunchy, just to start crunchy);  ditto fruits, especially apples. However, probably the only fruit juice that will help is the OJ with extra pulp.  

Orange peel is very good for fiber.  If you eat an orange, nibble on the peel when your finished.  If you eat toast, try marmalade.

So how does an oatmeal raisin cookie with some candied orange peel sound?

Oh, and drink lots of liquids, while you are at it.  The lower intestine can be too good at sucking out liquid.

question_title: What is the difference betwen a PC and a MAC, or Apple computer? Do they all connect to the internet?
question_content: Do PC and MAC or Apple computers function the same?
best_answer:
From a very basic level, yes, PC's and MAC's function the same.  They have an operating system, they run programs, they both connect to networks and the internet.

At a more detailed level, the operating systems are quite different and the inner workings of the hardware is, too.  But that's probably more detail than you need to know.

In general, people find MAC's easier to learn and more stable (less crashes).  PC's have more software available for them and are a little cheaper (usually).

Either way, they are both computers and do computer-type stuff.

question_title: Roman Catholics/Catholics?
question_content: Whenever I go through the Religion section in this forum and ask ,or reply, to points of religion people seem to 'deaf out' the fact that Catholics are Christians, even in some cases deny the fact. I would like any Catholic out there to tell me and the rest of this forum . Are you Christians in the full meaning of the name?
best_answer:
Catholics are Christians through and through--in the very fullest sense.  

People like to give (and make up) all kinds of reasons why Catholics are not Christians, but the one thing that truly sets Catholics apart most is the Eucharist.  Together with members of the Orthodox Church (the Catholic Church's "Sister" Church), Catholics are the only people who receive the Real Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity of Lord Jesus.  You don't get any more Christian than that!

Receiving the Eucharist literally transforms us spiritually into true sons and daughters of God.  That was the entire purpose of Jesus's Incarnation--He died so that we could be true children of God again.

That said, in order to receive the Eucharist, we must be in a state of grace (proper disposition, no mortal sins on our souls).  Unlike many Protestants, who think their salvation is guaranteed just by saying they believe in Jesus (regardless of their sins), Catholics care a great deal about making ourselves as worthy as possible, and we often go to great lengths.  This is because we know we are truly, completely, receiving Lord Jesus into ourselves through the Eucharist.  You wouldn't want to invite a guest into a messy house--we *definitely* don't want to do that to Lord Jesus!

It's no surprise that lots of Christians don't understand Catholicism--there is so much to learn, and not everyone likes to learn.  But no argument against Catholicism can stand up to Scripture or any other element of Sacred Tradition.  After all, the Bible is a Catholic Book (despite some Protestants thinking that the King James Version just fell out of the sky one day).  Protestants claim that Catholic Sacred Tradition "adds" to the Bible, but the fact is that the Bible IS Catholic Sacred Tradition.  

Finally, I'd like to address Catholics' veneration of Mary--which Protestants claim to mean that we worship Mary (and therefore, we are not Christians).  Veneration does not mean worship--it means honor.  As a good Jewish man, Jesus honored His parents (both Mary and St. Joseph).  Before His death, Jesus told St. John to regard Mary as his mother--which meant that Jesus was asking St. John to honor her as well.  So... who are we not to honor her?  Are we above Jesus and St. John?  Venerating Mary is one more way in which Catholics show obedience to Lord Jesus.  It should also be noted that at least some of the earliest Protestants (such as Luther) also venerated Mary and believed in her perpetual virginity.

question_title: up to one year? less than 1 year for misdemeanor?
question_content:
Which is right for misdemeanor?  Up to one year meaning 365 days or less than 1 year meaning 364 days?

Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of Law - Cite This Source 
Main Entry: mis·de·mean·or
Pronunciation: "mis-di-'mE-n&r
Function: noun
: a crime that carries a less severe punishment than a felony; specifically : a crime punishable by a fine and by a term of imprisonment not to be served in a penitentiary and not to exceed one year —compare FELONY 

Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of Law, © 1996 Merriam-Webster, Inc.
best_answer:
Such definitions are a matter of statutory law, not dictionaries.

What constitutes a misdemeanor, or a felony, is defined within each jurisdiction, state or federal, by statute. 

Generally, the phrase "not to exceed one year" means that one year (365 days) is OK, but more than one year (366 or more) is not. However, that is still a matter for definition within each jurisdiction.

question_title: I really find tough waking up in the morning :( what do I do?

I am a primary care psychologist who also interned in a sleep clinic.  Here are a few tips for good sleep hygeine that improve the quality of sleep and help people wake up feeling more rested.

Get into a regular sleep schedule that you keep even on the weekends.  Go to bed and get up at the same time every day.

Don't use the snooze button.  "Snoozing" is very poor quality sleep and only helps you feel more tired when you actually do get up.

Exercise is good-- not right before bed, but any other time of day works.

Limit caffeine, nicotine, and alcohol as all interfere with sleep quality.  

Use the bed only for sex and sleep.  No watching tv, no reading, no clipping your toenails :)  If you need some noise to help you sleep, use a fan or a white noise machine-- not the television.

One of the previous posters mentioned depression-- hypersomnia (sleeping too much) is a symptom of depression.   Here is an online depression screener that you might fill use: http://www.med.nyu.edu/psych/screens/depres.html

question_title: What are parametric and nonparametric data?
best_answer:
Parametric and Non-Parametric data

In statistical terms a parameter is a statistic calculated from a set of data, e.g. a mean or a standard deviation are both parameters. In order to calculate parameters, and to use them in statistical analysis three assumptions must be tested against the data. The data is considered as parametric if these three assumptions are valid:

1. Can it be assumed that the data has been obtained from a population which is considered "normal" in the statistical sense. In other words if a sufficiently large sample of data was obtained from the population is it likely that it would be normally distributed. This may be known from similar research, but if not, and provided the sample is reasonably large, it may be possible to estimate from the sample whether this assumption is reasonable.

2. The populations from which the samples are drawn should have equal variances. This can be determined by inspection of the data, looking at the spread or standard deviation of the data. The F - test can also be used to test the hypothesis that the samples have been drawn from populations with the equal variance.

3. The data should be measured, at the very least, on an interval scale. Even this is not always easy to determine, but a useful "rule of thumb" is to compare two scores, (say) a 5 and a 10, and to ask yourself if a score of 10 means that there is exactly twice as much of that particular attribute compared with a score of 5. If the data was temperature, then this is obviously the case, but what if the data represented a measure of patient satisfaction. A score of 10 may indicate more satisfaction than a 5, but not necessarily twice as much; i.e. this may be an ordinal scale rather than interval.

It is not always easy to know whether the data should be treated as parametric or non-parametric, and where possible always look at how other researcher have treated similar data. Of course it does not follow that they were correct in their assumptions, but at least if the research has been published, it will have been scrutinised by other researchers.

A further complication is that some statistical tests, e.g. the t - test is considered as "robust". This means that even if one of the assumptions is doubtful, then it is still possible to use the t - test.

If you have any doubts about the nature of your data, then it is safer to opt for the non-parametric test, because they do not require these assumptions of the data. Non-parametric tests are a little less sensitive than their parametric equivalent, and therefore they may not detect small differences between groups. You can't go wrong choosing a non-parametric test, but you may be accused of using the wrong sort of test if you choose a parametric test, when the nature of the data does not warrant it.

question_title: How many people died in Iraq under Saddam's rule?
question_content: Bush says 30,000 since we started the war.   iraqbodycount.net put it at 27383 (miniumum).  So are the Iraqi people worse off under Bush's war or Saddam's rule?
best_answer:
The most scientifically accurate study of civilian deaths since the war started was done by the Lancet, a British medical journal in 2004.

Based on the number of Iraqi fatalities recorded by the survey teams, the researchers calculated that the death rate since the invasion had increased from 5 percent annually to 7.9 percent. That works out to an excess of about 100,000 deaths since the war, the researchers reported in a paper released early by the Lancet.

At times it may have been worse under Saddam, but that was long before the invasion.  Saddam's worst killings were committed in the 1980s, including his gassing of Kurds at Halabja in 1988.  In Halabja 5,000 innocent civilians, 75% women and children were killed by Saddam's forces using chemical weapons.

It is hard to give you a solid number, because some surgeons I work with might do an knee replacement in a person with a hemoglobin of 10, while others would never do that procedure unless their hemoglobin was above 11.5 or so.  Also, the normal hemoglobin level is different for men and women, so these numbers are just hypothetical examples.

question_title: How far will it move in 2 seconds starting from rest ?
question_content: A shopper in a supermarket pushes a loaded cart with a horizontal force of 11 N.  The cart has a mass of 26kg.  How far will it move in 2 seconds starting from rest? How far will it move in 2 seconds if the shopper places his 30 N child in the cart before he begins to push it ?
best_answer:
So I'm assuming there is no static or kinetic friction in this problem.

Well, since the cart experiences a force in the horizontal direction, then: 
F = ma
a = F/m
a = 11N/26kg = 11/26 m/s^2

How far will it move in 2 seconds starting from rest?  What do we know?

a = 11/26 m/s^2
t = 2 secs
Velocity initial = 0 m/s (since it starts from rest)
So what is d (for distance although I know some schools use X)?

d = V(initial)t + 1/2at^2
d = 0t + (1/2)(11/26)(2)^2
d = 11/52*4
d = 11/13 m

30 N child in the cart before he begins to push it?

Newtons is just another way of saying weight but in order to find the acceleration we need mass and not weight.
Weight (in N) = mg
m = weight/g
m = 30/10
m = 3kg  <-------- this is the mass of the child

Repeat as above with little modification.
a = F/m
a = 11N/(26kg + 3kg) = 11/29 m/s^2

d = V(initial)t + 1/2at^2
d = 0t + (1/2)(11/29)(2)^2
d = 11/58*4
d = 44/58 m

Good luck!

question_title: How can I get rid of pimples?
question_content: I have just started getting a few pimples on my face and I can't get rid of them, any suggestions?
best_answer:
Wash your face thoroughly (until it feels tight and squeaky clean) with plain soap and water as hot as you can tolerate.
Do this twice a day. Pay especial attention to greasy sections of your face and rinse with clean water.
You do not need all those fancy preparations. They just add to the layers of guck in your skin.
Use a mild abrasive, e.g. one of those cheap oblong rubbery sponges that come ten to a pack. This will also give you a good lather from the soap.

Now, once you do this, you're likely to notice an increase in pimples. This is because you have cleared away skin guck to allow all the stuff underneath to escape. Don't worry - stick with it, it will be worth it.

When you get to the point that you don't have pimples any more, keep with the soap and water; it will keep the skin clean and prevent it clogging up again.

Lastly, if you have blackheads (common with acne, but not the same thing) buy a blackhead expresser to remove them. These are badly clogged pores and will turn septic if not cleared out.

question_title: hyper hydrosis--anyone else living with it?
question_content: Ive been embarassed by it my whole life any one have it or know what to do about it? (excessive sweating)
best_answer:
I have hyper hyperhidrosis as well.  It started when I was about 18 or 19.  I would come home from classes and my shirt would be soaked with sweat, no matter whether it was cold or hot outside.  Turns out my father has it too and I believe it's a genetic trait that's passed on.  I tried, in frustration, every deodorant and antiperspirant on the market to try to control it, to the point where sometimes I would just cake talcum powder on my armpits or actually scotch tape folded up tissues under my arms to keep me from sweating through my shirt.  I even tried abstaining from liquids, including water, for a long time in order to "dry" my sweat glands up.  Didn't work.  I ruined a lot of tshirts, pits stained with the salty residue of excessive sweating.  
From what I've read on the internet, there are really only three things that can be done to resolve the condition:
1.  Botox injections-botox can be injected into the area (in my case, armpits) to temporarily numb/paralyze the sweat glands.  Celebrities often have this done before they go out on the red carpet to avoid sweating in front of the paparazzi.  This procedure is costly and temporary; only lasts a few months.
2.  Surgery-the ends of the sweat glands can actually be burned off through surgery, thus ending the actual production of sweat in that area.  Costly, painful, and has the potential for later complications like infection.
3.  The most drastic resolution is the actual removal of the sweat glands.  Not only is this costly, but in can result in incredibly painful rehabiliation, infection, and all the other problems that can come from invasive surgery.

In my case, my hyperhidrosis started to disappear about a year and a half ago and I think it gets better with age.  I still sweat through my clothes sometimes, especially in a humid summer, but not as much as before, and I do sweat the sheets sometimes, but overall my case of it has gotten better.  Although I'm not sure if they're actually influential on the condition, I would see if maybe there are lifestyle changes you could consider that may help.  For example, if you consume a lot of sodium or other substances that cause you to retain excessive water, or if your diet is generally unhealthy or you don't get enough exercise.  I tried cool showers instead of hot ones for a while with mixed results.
There are several websites with information regarding hyperhidrosis.  I found my info on Webmd.com but some others you may want to look at are:
www.sweathelp.org
www.sts.org/doc/4097
www.handsdry.com
www.sweaty-palms.com
www.hyperhidrosis.com

You can just google "hyperhidrosis" and find several sites.  If you haven't already, talk to your doctor to see if their are any non-invasive treatments or new medicines on the market.  You may want to speak to your parents or relatives to see if they have ever had it (I'm not sure it's genetic, but in my case my father has it, I have it, and my brother has it as well).  I hope this information has helped and good luck with it.

question_title: Sets: need help please?
question_content: B is the subset of A, A is the subset of X. Prove X - A is the subset of X - B
best_answer:
You can start from the following identity for set differences which holds true for any sets X, A, and B

X − (A ∪ B)  =  (X − A) ∩ (X − B)

Now, if B is a subset of A, then A ∪ B = A

the identity above becomes

X − A =  (X − A) ∩ (X − B)

For this to hold true, X − B must be a superset of (X − A), or in other words, (X − A) must be a subset of X − B

question_title: What causes blushing?
best_answer:
What Is  Facial Blushing? 

Blushing results from an increase in superficial facial blood volume: blood vessels in the skin dilate, and red blood cells color the skin red. The area of skin that can blush is usually restricted to the face, ears, and neck, and in rare cases, the upper body. This dilation of the blood vessels is involuntary. Stress can increase the activity in the autonomic nervous system. Blushing appears to be an involuntary sympathetic nervous system response. 

Blushing starts at three years of age. At that age we become aware that others can observe us. Most people, however, do not remember blushing before the age of five. Normally, the intensity and frequency of blushing peaks in teenage years and decreases with age. However, even very old people can blush, and the amount of blushing varies greatly between individuals.

question_title: How do They Measure the Diameter of a Star?
best_answer:
In order to measure the diameter of a star you really need three pieces of information about the star (1) distance (2) brightness (3) and color.
Step 1: Scientists can figure out the total power output of the star by knowing its brightness at Earth and its distance. 

Step 2: Figure out the surface temperature. The universe really gave scientists a lucky break because stars are fairly predictable objects. What I mean is that, for most stars once a scientist know one property of the star they can generally figure out everything else they want to know about it. This is because stars behave like "black bodies". This is a physics term which describes how an object of certain temperature glows at different wavelength (thus influencing its color). Most ordinary matter resembles a black body (has nothing to do with being black, it's just terminology). You probably already have an intuitive understanding of this from your everyday experience. For example, when you heat up an object, at first it might start to glow red. And as it gets hotter it might start to glow yellow, blue, and eventually white. Because stars approximate black bodies very well, by knowing the color of the star scientist can figure out what its surface temperature is quite accurately. 

Step 3: Another great thing about black bodies is that, for any specific amount of surface area astronomers can predict exactly how much light it will radiate (hotter objects are brighter). And since they already know the temperature and the total brightness of the star they can figure out its surface area, and thus it's diameter :)

greek army what did they do, how did they fight, what did they fight with in the old days?
question_content: how did they fight, what did they use, what patterns did they stand in
best_answer:
Warfare in Ancient Greece centered mainly around heavy infantrymen called hoplites. The word hoplite (Greek ὁπλίτης, hoplitēs) derives from hoplon (ὅπλον, plural hopla, ὅπλα) meaning an item of armour or equiment and consequently the entire equipment of the hoplite (but not specifically the circular shield, which is sometimes incorrectly referred to as a hoplon, though it was in fact called an aspis). These soldiers probably first appeared in the late 8th century BC. These were a citizen-militia, and so were armed as spearmen, which are relatively easy to equip and maintain; mainly they represented the middle class, who could afford the cost of the armaments. Almost all the famous men of ancient Greece, even the philosophers and playwrights, fought as hoplites at some point in their lives.

How did they fight?
Since the hoplites were a militia force and did not receive permanent wages, campaigns were short and mainly confined to the summer. Armies marched directly to their target. There the defenders could hide behind city walls, in which case the attackers generally had to content themselves with ravaging the countryside as siegecraft was undeveloped, or meet them on the field. Battles were usually set piece and intended to be decisive. Both forces lined up on a level field, usually in a rough phalanx formation around eight ranks deep (though this varied). Other troops were less important; cavalry generally protected the flanks, when present at all, and both light infantry and missile troops were negligible.

With what did they fight?
Hoplites generally armed themselves immediately before battle, since the equipment was so heavy. Each man provided his own gear so it was fairly non-uniform, and often friendly troops would fail to recognise one another. A hoplite typically had a breastplate, a bronze helmet with cheekplates, as well as greaves and other armor, plus a bowl-shaped wooden shield called an aspis which was around 1 metre across. The primary weapon was a spear, around 2.7 metres in length; as this frequently broke upon charging and was unwieldy for close combat, hoplites also carried a smaller 60 cm thrusting sword called a xiphos. The total cost of the hoplon was roughly equivalent to a middle-sized car in our time.

question_title: I want to know about the transister its functioning and how it amplify the pulse provide in input?
best_answer:
The voltage, current and resistance are related by the equation, “Change in voltage = Change in current x Change in resistance.” 
If we have a device which changes the resistance without allowing a change in current then change in voltage is directly proportional to the change in resistance. Transistor is such a device. 
In an amplifier one gets an amplified output signal for a small input signal. Transistor is used in amplifier. It transforms the output resistance so as to keep the output current nearly equal to the input current. That is why it is called transistor. (Transforms resistor)
When a weak pulse is applied across the input of an amplifier having a transistor, there is a small change in the input current, voltage and resistance. But the transistor increases the resistance in the output, but keeps the output current same as the input current.
Current being the same, we get an amplified voltage.

question_title: what is "emangioma" and its treatment.is it a cancerous situation?
best_answer:
I am assuming you mean hemiangiomas.  The name comes from hemi (blood), angio (vessel) and oma (tumor).  Hemiangiomas are benign (not cancer).

 If you are talking about this hemiangiomas of the skin:
Hemangiomas are simply a collection of extra blood vessels in the skin.  Hemangiomas usually appear, grow and go away without problems. You can see pictures with examples of this condition here:  http://www.childrensspecialists.com/body.cfm?id=498

If you are talking about the liver:
hemangioma 
This type of benign tumor is a mass of abnormal blood vessels. Up to five percent of adults have small liver hemangiomas that cause no symptoms. Treatment is usually not required. Sometimes, infants with large liver hemangiomas require surgery to prevent clotting and heart failure.  http://www.luhs.org/health/topics/liver/tumor.htm

If you are talking about the spine:
Spinal hemangiomas are the most common benign spinal neoplasms, often located in the thoracic and lumbar spine, with a peak incidence of occurrence in the fourth to sixth decades. They are relatively common, found in 11% of autopsy series. Sixty percent are asymptomatic (cause no symptoms or problems).  without gender preference. Symptomatic hemangiomas are more common in women and present with back pain, radicular pain, or spinal cord compression. Acute symptoms occur from compression fracture, epidural extension and sudden mass effect, and hemorrhage.  http://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/446183_8

question_title: Increased activity of the sympathetic nervous system will?
question_content:
A. increase production of all hydrolytic enzymes by abdominal organs. 
B. increase only production of those digestive juices rich in buffers. 
C. have no effect on the digestive system. 
D. decrease production of digestive juices. 
E. increase movement of food through the alimentary canal.
best_answer: The sympathetic nervous system, when highly activated, causes stress-induced responses during times of danger.  So anything that aids skeletal muscle efficiency and motion will be stimulated.  So, blood flow will be directed towards skeletal muscle, nervous tissue, and brain, and away from everything else.  In addition to blood flow, all other systems will be inhibited (you dont want the intestines, stomach, kidneys, etc working hard while not getting enough blood flow).  So, the digestive systems and everything else will be inhibited.  If your sympathetic system is very highly stimulated, for an extended period of time, you will often get nauseous enough to vomit-because food will have been sitting in your stomach without being digested.  It may also cause diarrhea or constipation because of lack of digestive activity.\nGood luck in your classes.

question_title: what effects do your body get after a stroke?
best_answer:
If you have symptoms of a stroke, seek emergency medical care. General symptoms of a stroke include sudden onset of:

Numbness, weakness, or paralysis of the face, arm, or leg, typically on one side of the body. 
Vision problems in one or both eyes, such as dimness, blurring, double vision, or loss of vision. 
Confusion, trouble speaking or understanding. 
Trouble walking, dizziness, loss of balance or coordination. 
Severe headache. 
Symptoms vary depending on whether the stroke is caused by a clot or bleeding. The location of the blood clot or bleeding and the extent of brain damage can also affect symptoms. 

Symptoms of an ischemic stroke (caused by a clot blocking a blood vessel) usually occur in the side of the body opposite from the side of the brain where the clot occurred. For example, a stroke in the right side of the brain affects the left side of the body. 
Symptoms of a hemorrhagic stroke (caused by bleeding in the brain) can be similar to those of an ischemic stroke but may be distinguished by symptoms relating to higher pressure in the brain, including severe headache, nausea and vomiting, neck stiffness, dizziness, seizures, irritability, confusion, and possibly unconsciousness.

question_title: How did the dragonfly get its name ?
question_content: Why is the dragonfly called so ?
best_answer: "Where did the name ‘dragonfly’ originate? \nAnswer: We have not been able to find a definitive answer to this question. One interesting theory about its origin, however, can be found in a book written by Eden Emanuel Sarot in 1958 entitled Folklore of the Dragonfly: A Linguistic Approach. He theorized that the name dragonfly actually came about because of an ancient Romanian Folktale. In the folktale, the Devil turned a beautiful horse ridden by St. George (of St. George and the dragon fame) into a giant, flying insect. The Romanian names the people supposedly refed to this giant insect (when translated into English) mean ‘St. George’s Horse’ or, more commonly, ‘Devil’s Horse.’ According to Sarot, the peasantry of that time actually viewed the Devil’s Horse as a giant fly and that they may have started referring to it as the ‘Devil’s Fly’ (instead of Devil’s Horse). He stated that the Romanian word for Devil was "drac," but that drac was also the Romanian word for dragon. He thought that eventually the Romanian name for the Devil’s Fly was erroneously translated to the English Dragon Fly and this eventually evolved into the "dragonfly!"  "

question_title: where can one study for certification to sell or market insurance products?
best_answer: it is correct that each state has different laws on ins licensing-the best way one can study for a state insurance license is to interview with different ins companies- find one you have confidence in- that is to say--which one can teach you the  most about the ins business--not just enough to pass the state ins exam--that is not the most difficult part- who will train you about the ins and outs of ins selling and teach you how to counsel people and how to help people do whats best for them-that is financial and estate planning in its simplest forms- what co would you be proud to represent- that is ethical and honest in its marketing and sales practices--when i entered the ins industry in 1976 Connecticut General life had a reputation for great study and teaching of its agents, though it lacked some practicality in sales techniques--today consider the Principal Group- one of the largest ins cos around- used to be Bankers Life of Iowa--look at Prudential Financial- Connecticut Mutual-so many mergers have changed names and cos since the 80's and 90's- check around with some current agents and their cos- see if they are happy where they work- and what they thought of the co training they had--some cos have trainers to get you through the state exam only- then you are kinda on your own- sink or swim- other cos may have trainers on staff- to teach you about selling and counseling people on the uses of life insurance- for saving and retirement, like that- that is what you need- a co that will educate you and teach you about the ins business--not just help you get licensed and pass the state ins exam-- i am a retired independent ins broker, & a retired LUTCF, CFP, & CPA who spent 23 yrs helping people with life & health ins, and tax-deferred annuities and enjoyed my time very much helping others plan for their financial futures--good luck to you !! PS- in some states, like Tx, a co must sponsor you for the state ins exam-in other words they must hire you to be an agent for them and then help you pass the state exam to get started in your career--very important- check with the State Dept of Insurance in your state to see what the rules are to become a licensed ins agent--good luck to you !!

question_title: HELP! is there a law against your landlord opening your locked door with out consent?
question_content: The place I rent from will know on the door and if we dont answer they will unlock it and come in. Is there a law against this? I live in Michigan. Do you know a web page stating this law???????\n\nI have gotten an eviction notice for putting my dog in my apart for 15minuted while me and my mom packed my car.  We arn't supposed to have pets on the property but my mom didnt know this. and now we are being evicted... help!
best_answer:
There are local organizations to help you fight eviction.  The locked door is a different issue.  In a lot of places the law requires them to give you 24 hour notice to enter unless it's an emergency.  If you can't afford a lawyer, try your local Legal Aid.

Landlords violate laws frequently.  It's one of the most common legal conflicts.  Legal Aid or some other such organization might refer you to an organization that helps tenants in legal conflicts with landlords.  Legal Aid itself often doesn't have time for such cases, but they can usually refer you to the right organization.

On the other hand, the landlord's point of view seems reasonable, so you might have a hard fight if you decide to sue them. They don't want pets because pets cause damage.  They don't want to make exceptions because they don't want to have to decide which exceptions to grant.  So they have a strictly enforced rule.  Is the rule clear in the lease or rental agreement?  If it is, your case might be weak.   But if they violated a 24-hour-notice-to-enter rule or law, you might have a better case there.  Especially if you can get them to admit in writing or in court that they entered without 24 hours notice, or if you have enough witnesses.

My own personal solution to the 24-hour problem when I rented in the past was to have a very loud burglar alarm that would go off when they entered.  They soon learned not to enter without notice.

Whatever else you do, make sure the next apartment allows pets.

question_title: simplify  5x + 7y - x - 2y + 2x?
best_answer:
Like terms have the same variable (or have no variable).  In  this expression you have two sets of like terms: Those with x, and those with y
Those with x: 5x, -x, 2x
Add the coefficients:  (5-1+2)x = 6x

Those with y: 7y, -2y
Add the coefficients: (7-2)y = 5y

6x+5y  is the answer.

Hope this helps.

question_title: Are genetically engineered foods destroying our environment? How?
best_answer:
I guess it depends on which food and who you ask...

They genetically engineered corn to contain a toxin produced by Bacillus thuringensis, as I recall it, and figured that since corn can't cross-breed with any wild plants other than teosinte (believed to be the weed originally domesticated and bred into modern maize), there would be no bugs killed if the bugs didn't eat the corn.  Alas, the gene managed to find its way into weeds outside the cornfield, and was killing off the bugs where they were welcome.  Hence, we could seriously talk of environmental damage caused by the transferral of the BT toxin gene (by whatever means) to the other plants.

Conversely, if an genetically engineered crop allowed greater production of usable food from a given area of land, that would allow a greater amount of land to remain un-disturbed, or to remain in a wild state: there would be the potential for less encroachment on the habitats of other creatures, plants, etc.  Thus, there is equally the potential for protecting the environment.

There is really only one thing that I am totally confident about on this subject: we still have a whale of a lot to learn on the subject of direct genetic manipulation of plants and animals (as opposed to the genetic engineering that's been going on for several millenia, called cross-breeding and the like), and we're certainly going to have a lot of heartbreak and triumph both on the way to having an adequate understanding of this effort.

question_title: How many planets are tehre in universe? and their size?
best_answer:
As time goes on, we will be learning more and more about the planets that exist, and their size distribution. 

The really large planets are probably gas giants, from what we can tell. The smaller planets are rocky planets, probably. We use two main methods of detecting extrasolar planets:

1. Looking for wobbles caused by the extrasolar planet. 

If the extrasolar planet is big enough and close enough to the star, then the star will be pulled sideways as it orbits the system barycenter, and we can detect that. This method is mainly useful for detecting gas giants, like Jupiter.  

2. Looking for planetary transits

By looking for a pattern of repeating shadows caused by an extrasolar planet passing in front of a star, we can detect extrasolar planets. This transit method has not found as many planets yet as the wobble  method, but theoretically should be able to find much smaller planets, possibly even small rocky planets like earth.

There are several projects worldwide now (a couple of dozen or more) developing programs to find new extrasolar planets, so in the next few years there should be a large population of new planets found. So far, we know of about 150 extrasolar planets, most of which are gas giants. 

However, even if a lot of data are analyzed, from many many stars, using our best methods, our statistics will still be biased towards the largest planets, since those are the ones we can detect most easily. 

Some estimate that there might be planets around almost every star, and there could be several around every star, so there could be a LOT of planets in the universe. Very few will be in the habitable zone and of the right size for human habitation, but some probably will be.

question_title: how do I do this?
question_content: I need to know the molar mass, moles of each element, and atoms of each element. The element is Gold(Au). How do I find out this information? I already know the mass is 51.0617 grams.
best_answer:
Molar mass:  the number of grams in one mole (6.022 X 10^23 molecules) of a substance.  This is taken by adding the atomic weights of each of the atoms in a molecule.

Since gold is a pure element, its molar mass is equal to its atomic weight, 196.9666.

Since you have a given mass of 51.0617 grams, divide this by gold's molar mass to get the number of moles:
51.0617/196.9666 = 0.2592 moles

Now, since there are 6.022 X 10^23 (Avogadro's number) of molecules in a mole of any substance, multiply your number of moles by this number to get the number of atoms.
0.2592 X 6.022 X 10^23 = 1.5611 X 10^23 atoms

question_title: Can anyone help me reformat my external hard drive without wiping it clean?
question_content: I have a Western Digital USB external hard drive. Back in January, or earlier, the drive got corrupted and I can't access any files on it, which is my entire music library (3517 songs).  Is there anyway to uncorrupt it without losing all my music?
best_answer:
Lets explain first what file corrucy is...

All files are stored on the PC as binary (ZEROS AND ONES)
A file corrupcy is a damage in one or more of the binaries of the file making it unaccessible...


Normally, if the file header (which stores data abouit the file type, etc) is corrupted, in some cases, the file is recovered by doing a file header comparison to another of the same format (lets say MP3)...if the corrupcy is in the internal file, then this part won't work...(for example, the binary files for the segment between minute 2.35 to 2.47 is corrupted and won't be accessible by the Audio Player...

Purpose of file corrupcy and means of recovery...
__________________________________________________
Cause:
======
File corrupcy is either Physical or Logical...
Physical:
the hard disk fell or anything of the sort caused a physical damage to the media (BAD SECTOR)

Logical:
all these files were, for exapmle, downloaded from the internet...

Lets say you are downloading 2 audio files from the internet...one file is stored on the PC as 1,2,3,etc and the other is stored as A,B,C,etc

Normally, the files should be complete files, so, file#1 should be stored completely, and file#2 should be stored completely...

What happens when you download two files at the same time is that the Operating System stores a portion of each file after the other, so I end up having on the hard-disk both Audio files rather than being stored as:
1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 AND
A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I

I end up having:
1,A,2,B,3,C,4,D,5,E,6,F,7,G,8,H,9,I
So, for Windows to read the file, it has to keep on skipping segments on the hard-disk to load the entire file on the RAM to process and read...in some cases it fails to do so when there is a lot of segments to load...

Thats why Micorosoft included a tool known as Disk Defragment...it puts all these segments of the files after eachother to make files accessible and faster in processing...

Recovery:
=========
Logical:
Simply do a Disk Defragment...
Under Windows XP, right-click on the partition, choose Properties
Open the second Tab (Tools) and then click on "Defragment Now..."
On the new screen, choose the partiton to defragment, click Analyse, then after that, onc done, click on Degrag...

Physical:
You need to use a third-party tool to recover the data
Maybe Something like O&O DiskRecovery is what you need...it recovers data even if hte partition was formatted or damaged...
http://www.oo-software.com/en/products/oodiskrecovery/

How does this work..?
If Hard Disk was just formatted and not over-written, then the data still exist on the hard-disk in the System Volume Information Table...

If the Partition is damaged, it reads file headers and attempts to restore them
If the data itself is damaged, chances of recovery ar not 100%, but it attmepts to recover via Trial & Error

Hope this solves your problem...
Good Luck..

question_title: The No Child Left Behind Act?
question_content: I writing a paper and need to know what are your views on the NCLB Act. If you do agree or do not agree, why? What do you think could improve this?
best_answer:
The "No Child Left Behind Act": Pros and Cons
What are the Pros? 

1. Accountability - Schools and districts must demonstrate annually that all students - and all groups of students - are meeting state goals for grade-level work to be counted as making Adequate Yearly Progress (AYP). 

2. Focus on Children of all Backgrounds – Every state is now required to test all children in grades 3 through 8 and report scores broken down by race, ethnicity, low-income, English proficiency and special needs categories. 

3. Highly Qualified Staff – Sets specific requirements for teacher’s degrees and continuing education. 

4. Help for High-Poverty Schools – Title I schools receive both financial and technical assistance to develop and implement a school improvement plan. In addition, eligible parents will be able to transfer their children to other public schools if improvement is not met or get outside tutoring assistance for them.
5. It stirred the literacy program researchers to advise the reinstatement of phonics in early grades. They discredited the premise of whole language in response to low literacy rates.
Cons:
1. Freedom to Leave Failing Schools - While this is also a positive aspect of the No Child Left Behind Act, it may create problems in areas where many schools are failing to meet the guidelines. There may be no real choice in the end due to higher enrollment numbers in schools performing slightly better. 

2. Unrealistic Timeline – While many parts of the timeline set reasonable and realistic expectations as to improvement of student performance, other portions of the timeline may be impractical. For instance, teacher education requirements could be set too soon on the timeline for schools to comply. 

3. Unreasonable AYP Requirements – Adequate Yearly Progress is a vital part of any long-term plan, especially for the No Child Left Behind Act. However, some aspects of this goal may be unrealistic in cases of some special needs students and ESL classrooms.


 4. The federal law, "No Child Left Behind", and standards-
based curriculum clashed. It lead to "teaching to the test". Dire consequences for schools and teachers of "No Child Left Behind" affect curriculum through fear. Literacy program researchers retained much of whole language's jargon and perspective.
The "No Child Left Behind Act" is the most recent in a long history of system changes and education reform initiatives, some teacher-directed, others student-centered, this one test-centered.Democracy depends on the literacy of the majority, but success
has been elusive.

question_title: femme nue en action?
What are atoms?
best_answer:
An atom (Greek άτομον from ά: non and τομον: divisible) is a submicroscopic structure found in all ordinary matter. It is the smallest unit of an element to retain all the chemical properties of that element. The word atom originally meant a smallest possible particle of matter, not further divisible. Later, the objects that had been called atoms were found to be further divisible into smaller subatomic particles, but the word atom nonetheless continues to refer to them.

Most atoms are composed of three types of massive subatomic particles which govern their external properties:

electrons, which have a negative charge and are the least massive of the three; 
protons, which have a positive charge and are about 1836 times more massive than electrons; and 
neutrons, which have no charge and are about 1838 times more massive than electrons. 
Together, protons and neutrons form the nucleus of an atom, which is surrounded by the electrons.

Atoms can differ in the number of each of the subatomic particles they contain. Atoms of the same element have the same number of protons, but can differ in the number of neutrons, in which case they are called isotopes of that element. Atoms are electrostatically neutral if they have an equal number of protons and electrons. Electrons that are furthest from the nucleus are less tightly bound to the atom and are relatively easily transferred to other nearby atoms or even shared between atoms. Atoms which have either a deficit or a surplus of electrons are called ions. Particles in the nucleus also sometimes escape atoms, in a process known as radioactive decay.

Atoms are the fundamental building blocks of chemistry, and are conserved in chemical reactions. Atoms are able to bond into molecules and other types of chemical compounds. Molecules are made up of multiple atoms; for example, a molecule of water is a combination of two hydrogen and one oxygen atom.

best_answer:
x^2 + 10x = 7

Take half the coefficient of x and square it:

5^2 = 25

Add that to the equation:

x^2 + 10x +25 = 7 + 25
(x + 5)^2 = 32

Take Sq. Rt. of both sides:

x+5 = sqrt(32)

x = sqrt(32) - 5

sqrt(32) = + or - 4(sqrt(2) = + or - 5.65685425

x = 0.657 or -10.657

question_title: how do you go on a diet and lose pounds in 8 weeks?
question_content: i really need to lose weight so i want get picked on and have a boyfriend
best_answer:
Sweetie, I understand your pain. And maintaining a healthy weight is a good thing. But try not to pin your hopes for how the next year is going to go by how much weight you can lose. You only set yourself up for disappointment that way.

That being said, we all know that the way the body loses weight is when we consume fewer calories than we burn. See your doctor or another trusted adult and set yourself a healthy goal. If you're out of school now, you should have plenty of time to exercise (unless you have a job, but you still need to find the time). 

Pick a sport or an exercise that you enjoy. Swimming is one of the best ones you can do - it's low impact, helps develop those beautiful long muscles, and burns a TON of calories. I'm talking about lap swimming, now, not splashing in the pool with your friends. Although that would be far better than nothing. Exercise 3 days on, 1 day off, 2 days on, 1 day off. You have to give your body a chance to recover or you'll hurt yourself. When you exercise, go for 30 - 60 minutes at a time, but again, don't overdo. It's also perfectly acceptable to exercise for a short time several times a day. The point is to burn the calories.

After you get your exercise routine down, you need to look at what you eat. Write down everything you eat every day for a week. Include everything, even a stick of gum. Also, write down the time you ate it and what you were doing at the time. This should give you an idea of how healthy your diet is. Do some research on the internet for healthy eating, and plan accordingly. You should eat at least 1500 to 1700 calories per day - again, ask a trusted adult and DO YOUR RESEARCH on this part. You DO NOT want to get sick.

Continue logging your meals and exercise, and be sure to take a daily multivitamin and drink at least 8, 8 oz glasses of water every day. It may seem like a lot, but think of it as a way of flushing the fat out of your system. Depending on how much weight you have to lose, add another glass for every extra 25 pounds. 

Remember, this has to be a lifestyle change for it to be really effective. Good luck!

question_title: when you have a runny and stuffy nose.. where does all the snot come from? It is never ending?
question_content: when you have a runny and stuffy nose.. where does all the snot come from? It is never ending
best_answer: There are specialized cells (goblet cells) that line all of the mucous membranes of your body: nasal passages, throat, lungs, intestines, urinary tract, eyes, vagina and etc.  These cells are capable of producing and excreting copious amounts of mucus in response to infections, allergies, injuries, stimulation, and  nflammation. Most of the time this mucus you make is  your body's way of protecting and/or healing itself.  Mucus production also helps us rid ourselves of foreign invaders (bacteria, viruses, pollen, dust etc.).  In the case of a cold, plugging up the nose with mucus may help to kill the viruses by blocking the natural "air conditioning" and raising the temperature of the nasal membranes.\n\nMucus is mostly made up of water, proteins and inorganic salts.  Stuff that is readily available to your body, so it is no problem to make plenty.

question_title: Qui pourrait me faire parvenir un programmme d'entrainement pour le 10km?
question_content: Sachant  que j'ai 34 ans,1.80mètres  et que je pèse 72kg.Il y a 1mois que je cours(1à2fois par week-end).Mon premier test chrono sur cette distance est de 48min et 40sec.Je suis fumeur et ancien cycliste(environ 15 ans).Je pourrais rajouter une sortie de + en milieu de semaine.En esperant etre assez précis,merci de vos réponse.(j'ai un Polar.)
best_answer:
Le mieux pour progresser est de s'entraîner trois fois par semaine, pour un débutant comme toi. En gros (très gros), il y aura une séance avec des fractionnés courts (des répétitions de distances entre 300 et 1000 mètres) à l'allure à laquelle tu courrais ton 10 km ou alors vers 85/90 % de ta Fréquence Cardiaque Maximale (FCM) puisque tu as un Polar.

Une autre séance de fractionnés mais plus long (répétitions de distances de 1000 à 3000 mètres) à 75/80 % de ta FCM.
Ces séances sont à faire après un échauffement constitué d'un footing d'une vingtaine de minute et d'étirements.
Après la séance, il faut faire un footing de récupération et il est toujours bienvenu de s'étirer encore tous les muscles sollicités.
Ces deux footings sont a faire tranquillement (70% de FCM).

Une troisième séance sera un footing long d'à peu près une heure, en aisance respiratoire, c'est à dire tranquille (70/75 % de la FCM). Étirements complet par la suite.

question_title: how to convert rev/min to rad/s. please help?
question_content: I get an answer of 11.2 rev/min and this could be the problem to me obtaining the proper answer or it could be my conversions. please help! \n\nA playground merry-go-round of radius 2.00 m has a moment of inertia I = 230 kgm2 and is rotating about a frictionless vertical axle. As a child of mass 25.0 kg stands at a distance of 1.00 m from the axle, the system (merry-go-round and child) rotates at the rate of 14.5 rev/min. The child then proceeds to walk toward the edge of the merry-go-round. What is the angular speed of the system when the child reaches the edge?
best_answer: One revolution = 2pi radians.  One minute = 60 seconds.  So 1 rev/min = 2pi/60 rad/s.  Multiply 11.2 rev/min by 2pi/60 to get 1.17286 rad/s.

question_title: Homework Help - Algebra (Simple Interest Problems)?
question_content: John Craig invested a portion of $15,000 at 10% annual interest and the balance at 6% annual interest. If he earned $1260 for the year from the two accounts, how much did he invest at 10%?\n\nNot only I need the answer, please provide step by step procedure to approach the answer to this question. Thanks.
best_answer:
Choose x to stand for the amount invested at 10%.  The remaining amount would be 15,000 - x.  It's invested at 6%

Change the percents to decimals, multiply them by their amounts, and add them up to get the total interest:

.10(x) + .06(15000 - x) = 1260

Distribute the .06: .10x + 900 - .06x = 1260

Combine like terms: .04x + 900 = 1260

Subtract 900 from both sides:  .04x = 360

Divide both sides by .04: x = 9000

Find the other number:  15000-9000=6000

So, $9000 at 10% and $6000 at 6%.

Hope that makes sense!

question_title: What size bike should I get for a boy, 10, about 4'10"?  20 or 24?
question_content: I am getting it as a gift for christmas and don't want to tip him off.
best_answer:
It is important to note here that wheel size (20" or 24") really has little to do with the size of the bike except in very general terms.

A bike with 20" wheels will accelerate and handle much quicker than a 24" wheeled bike, while a 24" will be more aggressive in adverse conditions (mud, snow, etc) and be better for longer trips.

A 20" wheeled bike has 3 different frame sizes- Junior, Standard, and XL. A 24" wheeled bike has Standard and XL. This refers to the distance between handlebars and seat.

So, what size? In a 20" wheel, ask for an XL frame. For 24" wheels, get a standard length.

All this being said, if you go to a department store you will need to compare and find the right length frame which can be a pain but will provide him with the best fit and longest life... but do yourself a favor and visit a local bike shop.

question_title: Devil's tramping ground: do you know where it is and what the myth is?
best_answer:
The Devil's Tramping Ground
In a wooded area in western Chatham County, ten miles east of Siler City, is a well-worn path that forms a ring forty feet in diameter.  The path itself is a foot wide.  The center of the circle and the ground outside the path are lush with grass and other plant life, but nothing grows in the foot-wide track.  At sunset, when rocks or similar heavy objects are placed in the pathway, they are found the next morning to have been brushed aside.  In fall and winter, when rabbit hunters roam the surrounding countryside, their dogs perform joyously until the chase nears the barren circle.  Then the dogs tuck their tail between their legs and slink away.  They will not go near the spot.

Soon after the first settlers came to Chatham County, they discovered the strange site, which soon became known as the Devil's Tramping Ground.  This was before 1800.

Though no one ever saw him stalking there, it was believed to be the haunt of the Foul Fiend, who came at night to tramp around and around and around in a circle, his head lowered, his expression intense.  It was during these hours that Satan planned his evil schemes to undo mankind.  At the first light of morning he was gone, winging his way like a bat across the world to carry out his nefarious purposes.  Yet so scorching had been his footprints on the ground of his circular pathway that the soil became infertile, and the nocturnal retreat of the hellish Prince of Darkness was shunned and avoided.

question_title: Challenge: On a map with ratio of 4:10000, a road is 12cm long. a) How long is the road on the ground.?
question_content: b) What is the area on the map if the actual area is 3.2 km^2?
best_answer:
Part (a)
4:10000 scale means 4 cm distance on map represents 10000 cm or 100 m. Hence a 12 cm road is actually (12*100/4) = 300 m = 0.3 km long.

Part (b)
Length scale 4:10000 means area scale is (4*4):(10000*10000) i.e. 16:10^8. This means 10^8 cm^2 area will be represented by 16 cm^2 area on the map. Hence 3.2 km^2 = 3.2*10^10 cm^2 actual area is represented by (16*3.2*10^10/10^8) = 5120 cm^2 area on the map.

question_title: What is the main difference betweencovariance and correlation?
best_answer:
-- CORRELATION --

A measure of the degree to which changes in two variables are related.

The standard measure of correlation is the correlation coefficient, a number between minus one and plus one that indicates the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables.

A correlation coefficient of minus one indicates that they are perfectly negatively correlated, zero that they are not correlated at all and one that they are perfectly correlated.

Correlation risk is the risk that two variables or instruments are unfavourably correlated.

- - COVARIANCE - -

A measure of how two random variables behave in relation to each other.

Matrices of covariances are used in several different models.

It differs from correlation in that it incorporates measurements of the magnitude of the variations as opposed to the correlation coefficient which is dimensionless.

The correlation coefficient between two random variables is equal to the covariance between them divided by the product of their standard deviations.

question_title: Do you think the city has a bad effect on people?
question_content:
It's commonly held that city-dwellers build 'barriers' around themselves, both emotionally, mentally and, I'm presuming, physically.

People say that city life hardens you up, in an adverse way. It makes you distant, self-centred and obsessed with the materiality of things. (Commonly held views, not my own opinion).

Now I'm a country lad (UK, Dorset), at Uni in Exeter (a city) and so far I'm finding this to be true. Just wondering what anyone else thought?

No offence intended!
best_answer:
No, I don't think it has to be true.  I lived in downtown Philadelphia for about 5 years in my 20s and I loved it.  

When I first got there I was amazed by all the diversity, all the opportunities - so many things to do, so many things you could be.  As I got more comfortable in the city I found it to be the friendliest place I could imagine.  I could sit on the bus and strike up a conversation with folks next to me about any topic practically and came away, most of the time, glad for the personal connection.  I found myself in dangerous situations and as often as not I found that a stranger helped me out.

By the end of 5 years, I was burnt out and tired of the city.  Moved to the suburbs and very rarely went back (got tired of the parking problems, everyone in a hurry, sad to see the homeless and other suffering) but I think that had to do with my own life - the choices I made in where to live in the city, the job i had, the people I knew.

I think there is good and bad in everything and I think we would all do better to really look for the good in all thing and situations.

question_title: What is bio-informatics?
best_answer:
Bioinformatics is the application of computer science, mathematics, and statistics to solve biological problems.

A standard example is in virus drug resistance.  Sequence the DNA of someone's virus, then compare it (using statistical analysis) to other sequences that you know to be resistant to certain drugs.  If you find a match, then the patient is probably resistant to the same drug.

Another common application is data mining.  You take a huge database with thousands of pieces of information, and you search for threads of correlation.  This allows you to come up with relationships that are not apparent because of the sheer size of the data.
